title: Chain-level right-shift comparison of sheaf Hom complexes
statement: On a small ringed site (C,J,R), let K be the category of unbounded cochain complexes of R-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] and H:K^op × K → K the sheaf-valued Hom-complex bifunctor [def-pur-hom-complex]. For every integer n there is a natural isomorphism H followed by shift(n) to (identity × shift(n)) followed by H. No K-injectivity, boundedness, or derived-category assumption is required.

source.place: Section 21.34 (Tag 0A8X), definition and differential of the Hom complex; signed specialization of the parent shift calculation

proof.text: Obtain the product projections and their limit, differential and map formulas from homComplex_projections_exists. In degree k identify each internal Hom factor by postcomposition with the inverse of the target shift degree isomorphism. The helper productComparisonIso lifts these factor maps in both directions using Fan.IsLimit.lift; both inverse identities follow after all product projections. This constructs the degree isomorphisms without choosing arbitrary data.

Prove the degree-isomorphism projection formula by transporting the target index in a projection along XIsoOfEq. Check the chain-map equation using Fan.IsLimit.hom_ext and expand the differential on both sides with the specified projection formula. Postcomposition is linear in integer units, proved sectionwise by the two possibilities 1 and -1. The shifted postcomposition coefficient is n.negOnePow on both sides, and n.negOnePow * (k+n).negOnePow = k.negOnePow by negOnePow_add and units_mul_self. The proved additive-group helper shiftSign_sub closes the signed subtraction identity. Hom.isoOfComponents then supplies the chain isomorphism and its inverse chain-map equation.

Verify naturality of the chain isomorphisms degreewise and then after each product projection. Apply the same degree-isomorphism projection formula and the specified precomposition/postcomposition map formula. The component of a shifted target chain map in degree q is its original component in degree q+n, so the two resulting composites are definitionally equal. Assemble the natural isomorphism with NatIso.ofComponents. All indices and shifts range over all integers and no boundedness or injectivity hypothesis is used.

proof_origin.place: Section 21.34 (Tag 0A8X), defining Hom-complex differential; chain-level signed right-shift calculation formalized by B3, 2026-10-13.

lean.statement:
theorem homComplex_shift_right
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C]
    (J : GrothendieckTopology C) (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) (n : ℤ) :
    Nonempty (
      Functor.uncurry.obj (homComplexFunctor (C := C) (J := J) (R := R)) ⋙
        shiftFunctor _ n ≅
      (𝟭 _).prod (shiftFunctor _ n) ⋙
        Functor.uncurry.obj (homComplexFunctor (C := C) (J := J) (R := R)))
